scenes.title: Who Sits Where
scenes.text:
Seventh grade rearranges everything. {name} has a phone now, with a cracked corner, and the group chats sorted themselves out over the summer before anyone said a word in person.

The cafeteria has a map that nobody drew but everyone can read. {Poss} oldest friends still sit by the windows. The robotics club has taken over a table near the vending machines. The loudest table, the one everyone watches, has an open seat today.

Who {name} sits with this year will shape who {subj} knows at eighteen.

choices.label: {Subj} sticks with {poss} childhood friends
choices.outcome: {name} keeps the same seat by the window all year. It's comfortable, and the jokes go back to second grade.

choices.label: {Subj} joins a club and finds kids who like what {subj} likes
choices.outcome: The robotics club meets Tuesdays and Thursdays. {name} learns to solder and makes friends from three different neighborhoods.

choices.label: {Subj} tries to get in with the popular crowd
choices.outcome: {name} learns the rules fast: what to wear, who to text back, when to laugh. Some days it feels like winning. Some days it feels like work.

choices.label: {Subj} keeps mostly to {refl} and spends a lot of time online
choices.outcome: {name}'s closest friends live in {poss} phone, across three time zones. They're real friends, and the hallway stays a little lonely.

scenes.title: After the Bell
scenes.text:
By seventh grade, the hours between the last bell and dinner have become their own kind of sorting. Some kids head to practice in matching jackets. Some go to the band room or the robotics lab. Some walk to the rec center down the street, where the after-school program is free and the snacks are not great.

A travel team two towns over is holding tryouts. It plays tournaments most weekends, and the fees, uniforms, gas, and hotel nights add up fast. A few of {name}’s classmates have played on teams like it since they were eight.

At home, someone still has to watch the younger kids until six.

textVariants.append: {Poss} friends from the robotics table are already arguing about this year’s competition.

choices.label: {Subj} joins a school sports team
choices.description: Low fees, practice after school, and a bus to away games.
choices.outcome: Practice runs until five-thirty. {name} learns every teammate’s nickname and the exact smell of the team bus.

choices.label: {Subj} tries out for the travel team
choices.description: Families earning $100,000 or more spend about {stat:youth_sports_spending_high_income} a year on a child’s main sport.

availability.stretchNote: Families earning under $50,000 spend about {stat:youth_sports_spending_low_income} a year on a child’s main sport, and only {stat:travel_club_share_low_income} of their young athletes play on travel or club teams.

choices.authorFlag: The survey reports spending by household income but no price for travel teams, so this option is a stretch for the two lowest brackets instead of having a cost cutoff. Mapping those brackets to the survey’s under-$50,000 group is an assumption.
choices.outcome: Weekends turn into hotel breakfasts and tournament brackets. {name} gets better fast, and the family learns every rest stop on the interstate.

choices.label: {Subj} joins the school band or the robotics club
choices.description: Free or close to it, with an instrument rental or a team fee.
choices.outcome: {name} spends a lot of afternoons in a room that smells like solder or valve oil, with kids {subj} might never have met otherwise.

choices.label: {Subj} goes to the free program at the rec center
choices.description: Homework help, a gym, and adults who keep an eye on everyone.
choices.outcome: The rec center has a gym, a homework room, and a staff member named Denise who knows everyone’s business. {name} is there most afternoons.

choices.label: {Subj} watches the younger kids after school
choices.outcome: {name} can make three kinds of grilled cheese and settle any argument about the TV. Homework happens after eight.

researchNote.title: Friendship and Mobility
researchNote.text: Researchers mapping friendships across the US found that how often friendships cross class lines in a community is one of the strongest predictors of upward mobility there. If children from low-income families grew up with the cross-class connections of the average higher-income child, their adult incomes would rise by {stat:economic_connectedness_effect} on average.
